messages:
Joan (CS): FYI Middleshore reported search results returning in a different order than their upload when using Dedicated in us-west-2. They say it's reproducible and affects production ranking.
Mike (Eng): Can you share minimal repro steps + payloads? quick look first.
Joan (CS): They sent repro. Summary:
1) batch upload embeddings ids A..F
2) run top-5 cosine query
3) expected order A,B,C,D,E but got B,A,D,C,F
Sanitized curl they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/batch \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-xl-v1","items":[{"id":"A","text":"one"},{"id":"B","text":"two"},...}]}'
```
Query:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/query \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-xl-v1","top_k":5,"vector":[...]}'
```
They attached CSV mapping upload index -> id. They insist scores look right but ordering is off for near-ties.
Mike (Eng): Hosted vs Dedicated? Could be runtime/sharding difference.
Joan (CS): They tried Hosted sandbox and ordering matched expected there. Only Dedicated affected.
Ravi (SRE): Dedicated pool us-west-2-reserved-3 is running runtime v1.18.4 with kernel mode K-Auto. I'll pull logs for window 2025-11-02T09:10:00Z - 09:25:00Z if you need.
Mike (Eng): Ask customer for exact vectors or a redacted synthetic set that preserves score relationships. That'll let us run local repro against the Dedicated image.
Joan (CS): Uploaded vectors to ticket CS-9082. Linking in GH draft.
deploy-bot: Created issue infra/4580 (internal) and linked CS-9082.
Anya (Product): Customer is enterprise and ranking is core to them. Mark as high priority for customer impact. We need repro, regression test, and opt-in config for deterministic tie-break if that's root cause. Also add launch criteria: reproducible, test coverage, no P95 perf regressions.
Mike (Eng): Hypothesis: sharded query execution + subtle float nondeterminism across kernels or async commit ordering for large indices (>50k) causing nondeterministic tie-breaks. Plan: 1) spin up local dedicated runtime v1.18.4 image, 2) ingest their vectors, 3) run query 50x, 4) enable deterministic sort flag if available, 5) compare with hosted runtime image.
Ravi (SRE): If repro is confirmed, check worker sharding, quant path differences, and whether requests are served by mixed kernel versions. Also capture per-worker logs and exact timestamps.
Mike (Eng): Quick local commands I'll run:
```
# ingest
python tools/ingest_embeddings.py --endpoint http://localhost:8080 --file middleshore_vectors.json --model embed-xl-v1
# query multiple times
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/embeddings/query -d @middleshore_query.json | jq .results; sleep 0.2; done
```
If ordering flips between runs, we have a repro.
Joan (CS): Customer asked for ETA. Please advise.
Mike (Eng): Triage update in 48h. If we can implement a service-layer deterministic tie-break toggle, we can ship a config opt-in within one sprint (2 weeks). If it's kernel-level or quant precision, could be 3-6 weeks.
Anya (Product): I'll put a backlog item with acceptance criteria and draft customer comms. Also ask CS to gather frequency and whether specific queries always flip or only intermittently.
Joan (CS): I'll keep Middleshore posted and attach infra/4580 and ticket CS-9082. Thanks everyone.
